# Yundera/AppStore — Nextcloud

**Audit date:** 2026-08-01 · **Store version:** `nextcloud:33.0.3` · **Compose sha:** `b876aaf1749bde79873136f73e796adbcc0b65bd` (commit `0f5955e3e2`, 2026-07-10) · **Ref:** `main` · **Depth:** full · **Scope:** n-a (no `compose_base`)

## Headline

**ERRORED · top severity Minor · risk score 3**

The static leaf ran to completion. The functional leaf could **not** run: no demo PCS instance qualified. Per the binding Functional Review Protocol amendment of 2026-07-17 (rules 2 and 4), only a `✅ Ready` instance may be used, and on the Demo Management board both pool instances read `❌ Error`. This is an **infra** condition and explicitly **not** a fault of the app — the audit should be retried once a demo host is Ready. Because mandatory phases C/D/E/F/G could not be exercised, orchestrator Amendment B4 forbids `compliant`; the result is `errored` (retry), not a verdict about Nextcloud.

## Tech & Documentation (Static leaf — `LPwfKYUVig`)

Static verdict: **flagged** — 3 Minor fails, no Major, no Critical. `rationale.md`: **absent** (HTTP 404), and **not required** — no trigger applies: no service runs `user: 0:0`, no volume leaves `/DATA/AppData/nextcloud/`, no `privileged:`/`cap_add`, and authentication is enabled by default.

### Passing checklist items

- **No **`:latest`** on any service image** — `nextcloud:33.0.3`, `mariadb:12.2.2`, `redis:8.6.2-alpine3.23`, cron `nextcloud:33.0.3`. All four pinned. ✅
- `cpu_shares`** set on every service** — nextcloud 70, db 70, redis 10, cron 10. The field is present on all four (the tier choice is a separate Minor below). ✅
- **Volumes under **`/DATA/AppData/<app>/` — every mount sits under `/DATA/AppData/nextcloud/`, the `$AppID` form (`name: nextcloud`) that CONTRIBUTING mandates and its own examples use (`/DATA/AppData/immich/pgdata`). Nothing maps to a user directory or outside `/DATA`. ✅
- **Permission strategy — deviation rule D4 applied.** `nextcloud` and `db` declare `user: $PUID:$PGID`; `redis` and `cron` omit `user:` and therefore inherit `PUID:PGID` under Yundera's documented non-Docker-default behaviour. Effective uid is `$PUID:$PGID` on all four services and every volume is within `/DATA` → **D4 → pass**. No service runs `0:0`, so D1/D2/D3 do not apply; no `privileged:` or `cap_add`, so D5 does not apply. *Advisory:* CONTRIBUTING's literal wording (`user` must always be specified) is unmet on `redis` and `cron` — recorded as advisory rather than a fail because the deviation table keys on the effective uid, which is correct here. ✅
- **No hardcoded credentials** — every secret resolves to `$APP_DEFAULT_PASSWORD`, the platform-injected per-instance value. ✅
- **Static persistence check (mandatory core item)** — every actual state location is mapped under `/DATA/AppData/nextcloud/`: app root `/var/www/html` → `…/root/`; user files `/var/www/html/data` → `…/data/`; config `/var/www/html/config` → `…/config/`; installed apps `/var/www/html/apps` → `…/apps/`; **MariaDB datadir **`/var/lib/mysql`** → **`…/db/`; Redis `/data` → `…/redis/`. The database — i.e. the user/account/ACL store — is mapped, so the Ntfy-class unmapped-state data-loss hole is absent. ✅
- `post-install-cmd`** hygiene** — idempotent (guards with `grep -q Strict-Transport-Security` before appending; `occ background:cron` is idempotent), introduces no new image (operates via `docker exec` against the already-pinned container), and bash variables are correctly `$$`-escaped so compose-go does not interpolate them. ✅
- `name`** regex** — `nextcloud` matches `^[a-z0-9][a-z0-9_-]*$`. ✅
- **Documentation** — `x-casaos` carries a clear description in 6 locales, plus title, tagline, category, tags, architectures, author/developer, and `before_install` tips containing the admin credential table and first-boot timing guidance. Every volume line carries an explanatory comment. `icon.png`, `screenshot-1/2/3.png` and `thumbnail.png` all exist, and every asset URL points at `cdn.jsdelivr.net/gh/Yundera/AppStore@main/Apps/Nextcloud/…` — the canonical repo, not a contributor fork. ✅
- **Authentication enabled and documented** — Nextcloud's own login gate, auto-provisioned as `admin` / `$APP_DEFAULT_PASSWORD` via `NEXTCLOUD_ADMIN_USER`/`NEXTCLOUD_ADMIN_PASSWORD`, so no open setup wizard is left exposed; the credentials are documented in the `before_install` tips. This is an accepted alternative to the recommended AppShield/OIDC sidecar. ✅ *(static-only — the gate was not exercised live; see Functionality)*
- **Network isolation** — `db` and `redis` join only the internal `nextcloud-network`; only `nextcloud` joins `pcs`. ✅
### Failing checklist items

1. `pre-install-cmd`** uses an unpinned helper image — Minor.** The command `docker run --rm -v /DATA/AppData/nextcloud:/data alpine sh -c …` references `alpine` with no tag, i.e. an implicit `:latest`. The Tech Checklist item *Pre-install and Post-install commands security* requires specific version tags with no `:latest`. Fix: pin it (e.g. `alpine:3.22`). Severity Minor per the static leaf table (unpinned helper image in a non-secret context). The command is otherwise sound: it is idempotent (`mkdir -p`), and it legitimately runs as root because its entire purpose is `chown -R $PUID:$PGID` over AppData — the `--user $PUID:$PGID` requirement applies to commands writing to *user* directories, which this is not.
2. `thumbnail.png`** is byte-identical to **`screenshot-1.png`** — Minor.** Both resolve to git blob `84691c1249672f25c4581cc86e9342232e68a709` (544 827 bytes). The Documentation Checklist requires a thumbnail meeting the tile specification, and the static leaf lists *thumbnail reusing screenshot-1* as an explicit Minor. Fix: ship a purpose-made tile image.
3. `cpu_shares: 10`** on **`redis`** and **`cron`** uses the reserved tier — Minor.** CONTRIBUTING defines `10 — System Background (Reserved)` as reserved for system maintenance tasks. Neither service qualifies: `redis` is a hot-path dependency (the entrypoint wires it as `memcache.local`/`distributed`/`locking`, so Nextcloud's file locking blocks on it), and `cron` runs Nextcloud's background jobs. Under contention a weight of 10 starves the interactive path. The tiers the document itself implies are 70 for redis (datastore serving an interactive app) and 30 for cron (scheduled tasks). For contrast, `nextcloud: 70` and `db: 70` are exactly right — CONTRIBUTING names Nextcloud as its canonical 70 example.
### Advisory opinions (not fails)

- **Single shared secret (confidence: high).** `$APP_DEFAULT_PASSWORD` is reused for the Nextcloud admin, the MariaDB `root` and `nextcloud` users, and the Redis `requirepass`. This satisfies *no hardcoded credentials*, and the blast radius is contained (both datastores are off the `pcs` network and the value is generated per instance), but compromising the web admin password also hands over the database root credential. Distinct values would cost nothing.
- **Running the Apache-based **`nextcloud`** image as an arbitrary uid (confidence: medium).** The upstream image normally starts as root and drops to `www-data`; `user: $PUID:$PGID` bypasses that. The compose compensates with the root `pre-install-cmd` that pre-creates and chowns every bind-mount source, and `post-install-cmd` runs `a2enmod headers` afterwards, which suggests it has been made to work in practice. **This is precisely the class of thing Phase C/E would have confirmed, and it went unverified this run** — it is the strongest reason to retry.
- `OVERWRITEHOST`** is pinned to **`nextcloud-$APP_DOMAIN`** only**, while `caddy_1`/`caddy_2` also publish nip.io and sslip.io vhosts that are listed in `NEXTCLOUD_TRUSTED_DOMAINS`. Reaching the app over those hostnames may redirect back to the `APP_DOMAIN` host. Cosmetic, and unverifiable without a live instance.

## Cleanup

**Nothing to uninstall.** No install was attempted on either host, so no residue exists. The audit's browser page was closed; the two pre-existing pages belonging to the concurrent `functional-ClaudeCodeRoot-audit2` run were left untouched. Both demo instances are exactly as found.

## Verdict rationale

The static half alone would grade **non-compliant · Minor · risk score 3** (three Minor fails, no Critical, no Major). It cannot be reported as the verdict, because at `depth=full` a missing mandatory functional phase can never yield `compliant`, and Amendment B4 routes any errored mandatory phase to **ERRORED (retry)** rather than to a verdict about the app. The three Minor findings are real and actionable today; the functional standing of Nextcloud is simply unknown from this run.

## Retry guidance

Re-run at `depth=full` once the Demo Management board shows a `✅ Ready` instance with more than 1h remaining. The static half needs no re-work unless the compose changes. The three Minor fixes — pin `alpine`, ship a distinct thumbnail, raise the `redis`/`cron` cpu_shares tiers — can be raised independently of the retry.
